title: General-position isotopies of links
statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $L$ be a finite disjoint union of circles, $F\colon L\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ a smooth isotopy of oriented links (each $F_t$ an embedding, $F$ constant near $L\times\partial I$), and fix the projection $\pi$. Then for every strong neighbourhood of $F$ there is a smooth isotopy $F'$ in that neighbourhood, with $F'=F$ near $L\times\partial I$, such that the projected track $G=\pi\circ F'\colon L\times I\to\mathbb R^2$ has the following properties. (i) The vertical-tangency locus $\{(x,t): d(\pi\circ F'_t)_x=0\}$ is finite and has distinct times; (ii) the double-point locus of $G$ is a smooth $1$-manifold in $(L\times I)\times_I(L\times I)$, and its projection to the time axis has only nondegenerate critical points at distinct times; (iii) the triple points of $G$ are finite, transverse and occur at distinct times; (iv) each of the loci (i)-(iii) is transverse to the slices $t=\mathrm{const}$ except at the listed finite times, so for all other times the slice $G_t$ is a regular projection, the end projections are those of $F$, and between consecutive exceptional times the diagrams vary by planar isotopy.
strategy: Perturb the isotopy inside a finite-dimensional family with submersive evaluation (published tubular-target item). The conditions (i)-(iii) are open and are of finite type: (i) is the condition that the $1$-jet of $G$ avoid the codimension-$2$ stratum of vertical derivatives; (ii) that on the double-point locus the diagonal condition meets the $1$-jet transversely; (iii) that the triple-point locus meets the zero-jet transversely. Apply parametric transversality (Sard on the finite-dimensional parameter ball) to each condition in turn: the bad parameter sets are null, their union is null, and a good parameter exists; the resulting isotopy is $C^1$-close to $F$ and equal to $F$ near the boundary because the perturbation family is relative. This is the construction of Queffelec sections 2-3.2 and of the general-position step in Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo's proof; AC_omega is inherited from the quoted transversality theorems.

references.title: Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
